subject: Iceberg latency surge — customer impact, mitigation options, exec ask
messages:
From: Liz Harper <liz.harper@zentri.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@zentri.com, support+zentri@zentri.com
Date: 2029-05-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes — production impact

Rafael,

Over the past 45 minutes we've seen p99 latency jump from ~420ms to sustained ~3.2s, with an uptick in 5xx errors and a 10% drop in throughput. This is affecting our checkout flow; abandon rate is already up. Our SREs pulled a few traces (attached) — they show long queue waits before the first token is emitted. No deploys on our side.

Can Redwood confirm whether there was a routing change, concurrency cap enforcement, or any throttles applied to our pool? We need a short-term mitigation (even temporary reduced model fidelity or dedicated burst capacity) and a clear plan for a fix.

Liz
CTO, Zentri
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@zentri.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-01T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes — production impact

Liz — thanks for the data and the heads-up. I'm looping in Marissa (AC), Dev (SRE/serving), and Laura (ops lead) so we can triage immediately and propose mitigations.

Initial notes: our infra telemetry shows a localized sequence of queue depth spikes for the "zentri-us-pool" beginning 08:02 PDT corresponding with increased small-batch arrivals. There's a concurrent transient increase in backpressure signals from the ML worker layer and several request rejections that look like concurrency-cap enforcement kicking in for a subset of hosts.

Immediate actions I'm asking for internally:
- Dev: pull worker logs and recent routing policy changes, attach latest request samples.
- Marissa: coordinate SRE/Sales communication and confirm whether customer-facing incident advisory should be posted.
- Laura: evaluate on-call throttles and whether we can temporarily raise per-tenant concurrency cap for Zentri's pool.

Short-term mitigation options we can push in the next 20-90 minutes:
1) Temporary +25% concurrency cap for Zentri on the dedicated pool (fast, reversible).
2) Enable prefix/KV caching for common prompt prefixes (low-risk; may reduce per-token work).
3) Model fallback to the smaller inference variant (slightly lower quality, much lower latency).
4) Route a percentage of traffic to an adjacent region where capacity is available (requires routing policy change).

I will send an internal readout with logs and a recommended path in ~30 minutes.

- Rafael
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes — production impact

Quick update from infra: logs attached (sample_requests_20290501.log). Observations:
- Around 08:01-08:05 we saw a sudden influx of small, highly parallel requests from a subset of zentri-origin IPs; batching efficiency dropped drastically and a backlog accumulated on front-end routers.
- Several worker hosts reported "concurrency cap exceeded" and returned 503s while others continued to process but with elongated queue wait times (queueing at accept path, not model execution).
- No config rollouts in the last 6 hours; however, a routing policy we pushed last week that favors cost-optimized worker families may be moving a small fraction of traffic through hosts with lower burst capacity under certain load patterns. That interacts badly with spikes of many small requests.

Attached: sample_requests_20290501.log, routing_policy_diff.patch (small change to make routing sticky for dedicated pools).

Immediate recommendation:
A) Apply a temporary per-tenant concurrency override for Zentri (target +25%-50% depending on observed successful drains) at the pool control plane. This will reduce rejections and allow backlog to drain.
B) Flip on an emergency routing pin for the zentri-us-pool to prefer hosts with higher burst headroom for the next 2 hours.
C) If those don't reduce p99 within 20 minutes, push a staged model fallback for read-only endpoints to the smaller variant to cut execution time.

I'm standing by to implement A/B quickly if we get approval.

- Dev
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@zentri.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes — production impact

Liz — quick note from our side: we are switching Zentri to the emergency concurrency override now and pinning traffic to higher-burst hosts. Expecting the first signals of improvement within 10–15 minutes; we'll monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rate closely.

For transparency and exec alignment: 
- Potential user-visible risk: a temporary model fallback will slightly change inference outputs; if Zentri prefers consistent output, we'll avoid fallback and rely on capacity scaling.
- Commercial: we'll track credits if we need to spin up additional burst capacity beyond committed dedicated capacity. Rafael, can you flag whether this warrants an exec call for approval of an emergency capacity top-up?

On the customer comms front: I'll prepare a one-paragraph advisory to post in the status page once we confirm mitigations are effective.

— Marissa
Account Executive
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@zentri.com>, ops@zentri.com, procurement@zentri.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mortem & next steps — Zentri iceberg-latency incident (May 1)

Liz / Zentri team — thank you for your patience. Following the incident on 2029-05-01 we ran the actions described below and put a plan in place to prevent recurrence. Summary: the customer-visible elevated p99 and 5xx rate were caused by an interaction between a routing optimization (which occasionally places traffic on lower-burst host families) and a sudden surge of many small parallel requests from Zentri, which reduced batching efficiency and caused queue accumulation at the accept layer, triggering concurrency-cap rejections on several hosts.

What we did (May 1):
- Applied emergency per-tenant concurrency override and pinned traffic to higher-burst hosts; p99 dropped from ~3.2s to ~480ms within 12 minutes. (See dashboard snapshot: zentri_p99_dashboard.png).
- Flipped on prefix caching for the most common prompt families serving checkout flows — reduced token processing by ~15% for those requests.
- Deployed a conservative sticky-routing safety patch to keep dedicated pools on stable host classes under bursty small-request patterns (routing_policy_diff.patch).

Longer-term work (timeline):
- Short term (1–2 weeks): adjust default per-tenant concurrency heuristics to be more tolerant of high small-request fanout; add a backpressure signal to trigger early cache warm or model fallback before rejections occur.
- Medium term (4–6 weeks): enhance routing policy evaluation tooling to surface host-family burst characteristics before we push cost-optimization policies; add per-account simulation to forecast p99 under small-request spikes.
- Commercial: Rafael to follow up on any credit or burst-capacity invoicing; we'll propose a goodwill credit for the impacted hour and a discounted burst package for the next month if Zentri wants hardened headroom.

Attachments: zentri_p99_dashboard.png (dashboard snapshot), sample_requests_20290501.log, routing_policy_diff.patch.

If you want an executive readout, Markus and I are available for a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
